title: Seconds to Tour Points With Diagonal Moves
statement:
You stand on the first of a list of grid points, points[i] = [x, y], and must visit the rest in the given order.

Each second you move one unit in any of 8 directions: up, down, left, right, or diagonally (which changes both x and y by one). You may pass through later points early; it does not count as visiting them.

Return the fewest seconds needed to visit every point in order.

examples.why: To (3, 1): one diagonal then two steps right, 3 seconds. To (1, -2): two diagonals then one step down, 3 seconds.
Diagonal moves cover x and y together, so the trip takes max(2, 5) seconds, not 2 + 5.
The order is fixed: you must go out to (-2, -2) and come back, 3 seconds each way.

hints: The trips between consecutive points are independent. Solve one trip.
A diagonal step fixes one unit of x and one unit of y at once. Use diagonals while both still differ.

explain.intuition:
Because the order is fixed, the answer is the sum of the times between consecutive points. For one trip with horizontal gap dx and vertical gap dy, diagonal steps close both gaps at once until the smaller one reaches zero, and then straight steps close the rest. That is min + (max − min) = max(|dx|, |dy|) seconds.

You cannot do better: each second changes x by at most one, and also y by at most one, so you need at least |dx| and at least |dy| seconds. This is the Chebyshev distance, the way a king moves on a chessboard.
steps: For each consecutive pair of points, add max(|x₂ − x₁|, |y₂ − y₁|).
pitfalls: Using the Manhattan distance |dx| + |dy|, which ignores diagonal moves.
Using the straight-line (Euclidean) distance. Moves are on a grid and a diagonal costs one second.

solutions.title: Walk step by step
solutions.idea: Simulate the trip: each second step one unit toward the target on every axis that still differs.

solutions.title: Chebyshev distance per leg
solutions.idea: Each leg costs max(|dx|, |dy|): diagonals close both gaps together, then straight steps finish the longer one.

followups: You may visit the points in any order. Why does the problem become much harder?
Diagonal moves now cost 2 seconds. What is the time for one leg?
